entities.summary:
Lufthansa, officially known as Deutsche Lufthansa AG, was established on January 6, 1953, and has since emerged as the flagship carrier and largest airline of Germany, headquartered in Cologne. It plays a pivotal role in the global aviation industry, serving around 220 destinations across more than 80 countries, thus facilitating not only air travel but also international commerce and cultural exchange. Key figures such as Hermann Wilhelm Göring, associated with the original Lufthansa founded in 1926, and more contemporary leaders have shaped its trajectory, making it a significant entity in modern transportation history.

The airline's modern iteration was formed in the post-World War II era, reflecting the rebuilding of Germany and the rise of commercial aviation. Its first flight took place in 1955, and it became a founding member of the Star Alliance in 1997, which expanded global connectivity through cooperation with other airlines. Lufthansa has led advancements in aviation technology and customer service; for instance, it was among the first airlines to introduce in-flight internet services and has consistently received accolades for its quality and efficiency. The airline also played a role in economic recovery in Europe during the 1990s and 2000s, boosting tourism and trade.

Lufthansa's legacy includes its influence on global aviation standards and practices, as it set benchmarks for safety, efficiency, and customer service that many airlines now strive to meet. Its operations have impacted regional economies by creating jobs and tourism opportunities, linking cities and cultures across Europe and beyond. The airline has faced challenges, such as the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, which resulted in significant operational changes and adaptations. Still, it continues to symbolize resilience and innovation in the airline industry.
